highlights: Frontier models continue to advance with major releases from Google (Gemini 4 Argon), Meta (Muse Spark Open MoE), and MiniMax (M3.1 Flash MoE), emphasizing multimodal capabilities, open-weight accessibility, and competitive pricing for large agentic models.

The tooling landscape for AI agents and GPU orchestration is rapidly maturing, marked by NVIDIA open-sourcing Run:ai for Kubernetes GPU management and Google releasing Harness2 for recursive agent performance enhancement.

Practical applications and efficiency gains for AI are increasingly evident, from Stack Overflow's agent plugin tripling signups to new tutorials enabling zero-training tabular predictions, highlighting tangible value for builders and enterprises.

agents.title: Amp Puts AI Agents to Work Beyond Code with OpenAI Models
agents.summary: Amp demonstrates how it leverages OpenAI's advanced models (GPT-6 Astra, Ultrafast, GPT-Live-1) to significantly expand the capabilities of AI agents beyond traditional coding tasks, enabling new frontiers for agentic applications.

agents.title: Third Moment Research Runs 10,000 Agents for 36+ Hours
agents.summary: Third Moment Research utilizes OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to build agents capable of sustained focus and improvement over days, showcasing advancements in scalable, long-duration agentic operations for complex tasks like cybersecurity.

agents.title: Run Fast, Private Agents On-Device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
agents.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a model enabling rapid, private, on-device AI agents. This development is crucial for applications requiring high privacy and low latency, moving agentic AI closer to edge deployments.

models.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to Solve Your Hardest Problems
models.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, their latest frontier model, offering advanced capabilities to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers for tackling highly complex challenges.

models.title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: Open-Weight Multimodal MoE from Meta
models.summary: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight, multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) frontier model. This provides builders with a powerful, customizable, and scalable foundation for advanced multimodal AI applications.

models.title: MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input
models.summary: MiniMax launched M3.1 Flash, a 428B MoE model with 23B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. Priced competitively at $0.15/M input tokens, it offers a powerful agentic foundation for high-scale applications.

tools.title: NVIDIA Open Sources Run:ai Under Apache 2.0 for Kubernetes GPU Orchestration
tools.summary: NVIDIA has open-sourced its Run:ai GPU orchestration platform under Apache 2.0, providing developers with advanced tools for managing and fractionalizing GPU resources in Kubernetes environments, including KAI Scheduler and CUDA 13.4 support.

tools.title: Google Open-Sources Harness2, a Recursive Agent Harnessing Framework
tools.summary: Google Research open-sourced Harness2, an Apache-2.0 framework designed to dynamically rewrite an agent's harness during testing. This significantly boosts agent performance, exemplified by an 11.5-point lift on GLM-5 for WorkBuddy-Bench without model weight updates.

tools.title: TorchNeuron: Running HF Models on AWS Trainium Is Easier Than Ever
tools.summary: Hugging Face announced TorchNeuron, simplifying the deployment and optimization of Hugging Face models on AWS Trainium hardware. This streamlines the process for developers leveraging AWS for high-performance AI inference and training.

companies.title: Stack Overflow for Agents Triples Signups with ChatGPT Plugin
companies.summary: Stack Overflow for Agents leveraged a ChatGPT plugin to achieve significant growth, tripling signups and driving up to 10x growth in agent creation, demonstrating the power of ecosystem integrations for accelerating AI agent development.

companies.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to Academic Research Labs
companies.summary: OpenAI introduced the Rosalind Academic Plan, offering eligible academic labs sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind and associated tools. This initiative aims to accelerate life sciences research by democratizing access to powerful AI capabilities.

companies.title: Google Beam Expands with New Regions, Partners, and Customers
companies.summary: Google's Beam initiative is expanding into five new countries and forming partnerships, signaling significant growth and increased accessibility for its service. This indicates wider adoption and potential for new AI-powered applications across more regions.

learning.title: How to Make Zero-Training Tabular Predictions with NVIDIA Structured Data Models
learning.summary: This tutorial guides developers on implementing NVIDIA’s new Structured Data Models library, enabling zero-training tabular predictions using pretrained foundation models like TabICLv2 and KumoTabular via a PyTorch interface.

learning.title: Teaching Students to Think and Learn Through Questions
learning.summary: This educational initiative promotes active, step-by-step learning using AI for Educators in Brazilian Portuguese and features Study Mode, highlighting methods to support students in developing critical thinking skills through AI-powered questioning.

learning.title: DevFest is Back: Build, Secure, and Scale in the Agentic AI Era
learning.summary: DevFest 2026 is announced, inviting developers to connect with over 800 global events focused on building, securing, and scaling applications in the agentic AI era. This provides a key learning and networking opportunity for the developer community.
